messages:
Ivy (marketing): hey team — prepping a technical sidebar for the launch blog. need a quick sanitypack to validate our qualitative claim about long-context tail stability on hero-pro. specifically: interleaved sessions where one session primes a 6k token context then another session hits the model (session handover). want to show warmed-session p95 + a jitter metric (p99-p50) for long-gen. can runtime run a small matrix?

Kaden (runtime): interesting. clarify 'session handover' — do you mean keep KV cache warm for session A then switch traffic to session B without reloading weights, or fully isolate sessions?

Ivy (marketing): keep weights hot; KV cache should be primed by session A, then session B should run independent prompts that benefit from shared kernel/weight hotness but not the same KV context. goal is to show production-like interleaving. acceptance: warmed p95 <= 450ms and jitter (p99-p50) < 220ms for warmed long-gen on recommended int8 variant. if not, we fallback to conservative language.

Marta (eng-runtime): plan: tiny matrix — cold baseline (no cache) 300 requests seq=4096, warmed primed cohort (prime=6000 tokens by session A, then 200 session-B requests) with int8-llm and awq-int8 and fp16. also include a short handover burst: after priming, send 30 rps for 30s of interleaved new sessions. outputs: CSV, percentile summary, jitter numbers, 5 raw json examples per cell, and runbook. est ~2 hours.

Ethan (product): please include minimal quality checks on the 5 samples (length, truncated sentences). also add a tiny BLEU-lite diff vs baseline so we can flag big regressions.

Kaden (runtime): sample payload for session A priming:
```json
{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."}
{"prompt":"Detailed release notes: <~6000 tokens>"}
```
session B sample:
```json
{"prompt":"Summarize release notes in 4 bullets","context":"short followup prompt unrelated to prime content"}
```

Kaden (runtime): sample CLI well run:
```bash
# cold baseline
curl -s -X POST https://bench.internal/run -d '{"model":"hero-pro","variant":"fp16","requests":300,"seq":4096}'
# primed handover
curl -s -X POST https://bench.internal/run -d '{"model":"hero-pro","variant":"int8-llm","prime":6000,"handover_target_requests":200,"handover_interleave":true,"traces":true}'
# burst handover
curl -s -X POST https://bench.internal/run -d '{"model":"hero-pro","variant":"awq-int8","prime":6000,"burst_rps":30,"burst_dur_s":30,"handover_interleave":true}'
```

Kaden (runtime): Q: warm weights between variant runs? that will show steady-state. cold restart per variant shows worst-case.

Ivy (marketing): prefer warm weights between variants to reflect production ops. keep cold cohort strict no-cache. document everything in runbook.

Marta (eng-runtime): noted. also: if we observe p99 spikes > 1s or jitter > 220ms on int8 variants, we'll auto-trigger a reproducible 5k run with fixed seeds to rule out outliers.

bench-bot: bench-job-2278901234 queued by Kaden at 2026-03-23T10:02:00Z

Priya (docs): docs may pick one warmed sample for the sidebar screenshot. please redact internal links/IDs and mark the sample as docs-safe.

Ivy (marketing): perfect. can you please post artifacts + one-line PASS/FAIL against acceptance by EOD+1? if timing tight we can accept morning+2 but need results before content freeze. thanks all :sparkles:
